title: Share Trading Policy

tiers.name: Mesoblast Personnel
tiers.description: Each director, company secretary, officer and employee of the Mesoblast Group of Companies, and each contractor and consultant to the Group.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors and the company secretary; direct reports to the CEO; and any other person notified by the CEO, Chairman or company secretary that they are subject to this policy. Must comply with the general clause 3 rules and are subject to additional dealing-notification obligations.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: In relation to a Designated Person: their spouse; children (including step-children) under 18; their nominee, including an investment manager managing funds on their behalf; a trust of which they, a family member, or a family-controlled company is trustee or beneficiary; a partner acting as such; and a company they or their family control. Connected Persons are themselves Designated Persons and so are bound by the clause 3 rules.

windows.end_anchor: announcement of the Company's preliminary annual report (Appendix 4E) plus 2 calendar days
announcement of the Company's half year report (Appendix 4D) plus 2 calendar days

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board, via the Company Secretary or Chairman, may declare further prohibited trading periods from time to time, for example when the Company is embarking on a significant unannounced transaction or development. Confidentiality of such periods is not addressed.

rules.detail: Absolute, one-line ban on trading in 'the Company's derivatives', with no clearance route, no vesting distinction and no definition of 'derivatives' given; on its natural reading it covers any derivative referencing the Company's securities, not only Company-issued instruments, so an OTC put and call with a bank would be caught.
rules.evidence: Mesoblast Personnel must not trade in the Company's derivatives.

rules.detail: Connected Persons of a Designated Person (spouse, minor children, nominee/investment manager, trust, controlled company, partner) are themselves Designated Persons and must comply with clause 3, including the derivatives ban.
rules.evidence: These persons in paragraphs (a) to (d) are referred to in this policy as "Designated Persons" and must comply with the Policy as outlined in clause 3.

rules.detail: 'Hedging' is not a defined or named concept anywhere in the policy, but any hedge implemented through a derivative (such as a purchased put or written call) falls within the absolute ban on trading in the Company's derivatives.
rules.evidence: Mesoblast Personnel must not trade in the Company's derivatives.

rules.detail: Monetisation structures (e.g. prepaid forwards) are not named, but such a structure is itself a derivative and so falls within the clause 3.3 ban.
rules.evidence: Mesoblast Personnel must not trade in the Company's derivatives.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named, but a CFD referencing the Company's shares is a derivative and so falls within the clause 3.3 ban.
rules.evidence: Mesoblast Personnel must not trade in the Company's derivatives.

rules.detail: Margin lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge over Company securities is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Secured financing arrangements in respect of Company securities are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
No minimum holding period, short-term intention test or similar rule is stated.

clearance.evidence: Mesoblast Personnel will not be given clearance to deal in securities of the Company under this policy where price sensitive, non-public information exists in relation to a matter, even though they may not be aware of it.

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary, who notifies the ASX
clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days after the change (Company notifies ASX within 5 business days)
clearance.evidence: Each of the directors is required to notify the company secretary within two business days after any change in their interests in securities of the Company, or the interests of any of their Connected Persons listed above.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 5 business days of effecting the dealing
clearance.evidence: All other Designated Persons are required to notify the company secretary of any dealing in securities of the Company within five business days of effecting such a dealing.

exceptions.evidence: dealing in a managed securities portfolio where the Mesoblast Personnel is not in a position to influence a choice of the portfolio
dealing under a dividend reinvestment plan where the Mesoblast Personnel has given a standing instruction to reinvest dividends

conversion of options to shares on exercise of options granted under the Mesoblast Employee Share Option Plan (however any trading in shares required to fund the exercise of options is NOT an exception and is covered by this policy).

exemption_authority: None. There is no hardship, court-order or other discretionary waiver from the black-out periods or the derivatives ban; only the fixed exceptions in clause 3.6 (managed portfolios, dividend reinvestment plans, option exercise) apply, and the Board's power under 3.5(c) is only to add further blackout periods, not to grant relief from them.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Mesoblast Personnel must not trade in the Company's derivatives.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This one-line, undefined and unconditional prohibition applies to every director, officer, employee, contractor and consultant (and their Connected Persons) at all times, with no clearance mechanism and no vesting distinction, and on a natural reading blocks the purchased put and written call legs of a bank collar outright.

bespoke_clauses.clause: No provision of the policy refers to margin lending, security, charges, pledges or any other secured financing arrangement in respect of Company securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar (secured on the collared shares) is not expressly prohibited or regulated by this policy at all, so absent the derivatives ban it would not itself be a policy obstacle; however, since the derivative legs are banned, the financing leg cannot be isolated into a compliant transaction.

bespoke_clauses.topic: trust/company structuring does not avoid insider trading
bespoke_clauses.clause: the definition of "procure" can include a director or employee who acquires Company securities through a trust or company while in possession of "inside information" may contravene these insider trading provisions and this Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Structuring the collar or loan through a personal trust or holding company does not avoid personal liability if the individual is in possession of inside information at the time, and Connected Persons (including such trusts and controlled companies) are independently bound by the clause 3 rules including the derivatives ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy was adopted by the Mesoblast Board of Directors on 28 August 2013.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The document provided is dated 2013 with no amendment history or next-review date recorded; a bank should confirm this remains Mesoblast's current, in-force Share Trading Policy before relying on its terms.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for any Mesoblast Personnel or their Connected Persons. Clause 3.3 imposes an absolute, unconditional and undefined ban on trading in 'the Company's derivatives', with no clearance mechanism, no exception in clause 3.6, no vesting distinction, and no discretionary waiver authority anywhere in the document, so the purchased put and written call legs of an OTC collar are prohibited outright regardless of whether the shares are vested. This ban extends to a Designated Person's spouse, minor children, nominee or investment manager, family trust, or family-controlled company, so routing the derivative through an associate does not avoid it. By contrast, the loan leg is entirely unaddressed: the policy contains no provision on margin lending, encumbrance or secured financing, so a standalone secured loan (without the derivative overlay) would not itself breach this policy. Because the collar's option legs are banned, the structure as a whole cannot be implemented, and any attempt to acquire the securities or deal via a trust or company while in possession of inside information would separately risk an insider trading contravention. The document is dated 2013 with no evidence of subsequent amendment, so its current force should be confirmed before relying on it.
